subtopics.title: Closing Off: Trading and Profit and Loss

questions.question: The trading account of Khumalo and Smit Traders shows sales of R2 856 000 and cost of sales of R1 904 000. Gross profit is:
options: R952 000 — exactly 50 percent on cost, matching the mark-up policy

questions.question: The profit and loss account gathers, on its credit side:
options: Gross profit R952 000 plus operating incomes of R76 000

questions.question: With operating expenses of R526 000 and interest on loan of R22 000 against R1 028 000 of credits, net profit is:
In a partnership, net profit closes off to:
options: The appropriation account, where the agreement divides it

questions.question: The order in which the agreement is executed in the appropriation account is:
options: Interest on capital, then salaries and bonus, then the remaining profit in the ratio two to one
Whatever order the partners prefer each year

questions.question: After appropriating R360 000 of the R480 000 net profit, the remaining R120 000 is shared two to one, giving:
options: R80 000 to Khumalo and R40 000 to Smit
R90 000 to Khumalo and R30 000 to Smit
R40 000 to Khumalo and R80 000 to Smit

questions.question: Smit's total earnings for the year — interest R20 000, salary R156 000, bonus R12 000, profit share R40 000 — come to:
A partner's salary belongs in:
options: Operating expenses in the profit and loss account
The appropriation account — it is a distribution of profit, never an expense

subtopics.title: The Current Accounts in the Ledger

questions.question: Khumalo's current account: opening credit R9 600, earnings R252 000, drawings R214 000. The closing balance is:
options: R47 600 credit — the business owes Khumalo R47 600

questions.question: Smit's current account opens with R6 300 on the debit side. This means:
options: Last year she drew more than she earned, so she owed the business R6 300
Her capital was reduced by R6 300
An error was made last year

questions.question: Smit's closing balance, after credits of R228 000 against the old R6 300 plus drawings of R195 500, is:
Which item never appears in a current account?
options: A capital contribution — that belongs in the fixed capital account

questions.question: Khumalo takes trading stock of R4 200 for personal use. The effects are:
options: Assets down R4 200; equity down R4 200 through drawings at cost; liabilities unchanged
Assets up R4 200; equity up R4 200
Assets down R4 200; liabilities down R4 200
Equity down R4 200; liabilities up R4 200

questions.question: Interest on capital allowed to a partner changes total equity by:
options: A decrease equal to the interest
Nothing — it redistributes equity from the profit pool to the partner's current account claim
An increase equal to the interest

questions.question: Interest of R22 000 capitalised on the loan affects the equation as:
options: Assets down R22 000, liabilities down R22 000
Assets up R22 000, equity up R22 000
Liabilities up R22 000, equity down R22 000, assets untouched
No effect anywhere, since no cash moved

questions.question: The reliable method for equation analysis is:
options: Guess the effects from the story
Write the double entry first, classify each account, then read the effects off the debits and credits

questions.question: The three ladles serve the profit pot in the order:
options: Interest for the money that waited, salaries and bonus for the hands that worked, then the leftovers split for risk
Leftovers first, then interest, then salaries
Equal shares to each partner, three times

questions.question: Paying bigger partner salaries changes the size of the profit pot by:
options: Nothing — the ladles serve profit after it is measured; they never shrink it
Shrinking it only if paid in cash

questions.question: The recipe that ends the argument at the pot is:
options: The partnership agreement, written before the cooking started

questions.question: The servings from the appropriation account land on:
options: Each partner's tab — the current account — not in an envelope of cash
The capital account on the wall

questions.question: A tab that goes red during a year tells you:
options: The partner took out more than they earned that year

questions.question: Smit earned R228 000 and drew R195 500 against an opening red tab of R6 300. Her tab now shows:
While the tabs rose and fell all year, the capital on the wall:
Smit contributes R60 000 by EFT. The scale reads:
options: Bank up sixty, owners' side up sixty — level
Bank up sixty, outsiders' side up sixty

questions.question: Stock taken home by a partner is priced at:
options: Selling price, because stock normally sells
Cost, through drawings — no customer bought anything
Whatever the partner offers to pay

questions.question: The event that makes the shop poorer without the bank balance moving is:
options: Interest capitalised on the loan — outsiders' side up, owners' side down

questions.question: Sharing the pot between partners affects the total owners' side by:
options: Reducing it by the interest on capital
Increasing it by the profit shares
Nothing — it just writes names on the servings
